verses.text: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that Yahweh’s word  by Jeremiah’s mouth might be accomplished, Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,
“Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, ‘Yahweh, the God  of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

Whoever there is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of Yahweh, the God of Israel (he is God), which is in Jerusalem.

Whoever is left, in any place where he lives, let the men of his place help him with silver, with gold, with goods, and with animals, besides the freewill offering for God’s house which is in Jerusalem.’”
Then the heads of fathers’ households of Judah and Benjamin, the priests, and the Levites, all whose spirit God had stirred to go up rose up to build Yahweh’s house which is in Jerusalem.
All those who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with animals, and with precious things, besides all that was willingly offered.
Also Cyrus the king brought out the vessels of Yahweh’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out of Jerusalem, and had put in the house of his gods;
even those, Cyrus king of Persia brought out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
This is the number of them: thirty platters of gold, one thousand platters of silver, twenty-nine knives,
thirty bowls of gold, four hundred ten silver bowls of a second sort, and one thousand other vessels.
All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up when the captives were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

footnotes.content: The God who spoke through Jeremiah—who saw exile coming and promised return—He stirred up a pagan king's heart without Cyrus even knowing his name. Grace works through unlikely servants, turning a Persian decree into God's answer to seventy years of prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cyrus speaks as though Yahweh has commissioned him personally. Whether or not he grasped it, he spoke truth: the God of heaven does command, and His purposes move kings. We live in a world where unseen hands guide the hearts of the powerful toward the good God intends.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An open invitation—"whoever there is among you." After seventy years in exile, some had built homes in Babylon, raised children, put down roots. The call to rebuild cost something: comfort, safety, the known. Yet God's blessing followed the willing heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king's generosity—even those who stayed behind were to help with silver and gold. Cyrus ensured the returnees were equipped, not left empty-handed. There's gentleness here, a care in the practicalities of rebuilding. Sometimes God grants us just what we need through unexpected sources.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The heads of fathers' households rose first—the keepers of memory, the ones who remembered the temple they had lost. They led their families forward because God stirred their spirits. Faith that moves a whole people begins with leaders whose hearts are open to His call.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who stayed strengthened the hands of those who went. Silver, gold, beasts, precious things—a community pooled what they had. The work of God is rarely a solitary journey; it moves on the prayers, gifts, and sacrifices of the faithful gathered around us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cyrus brought out the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had plundered seventy years before. The God who lets His house be stripped does not forget it. He restores what was lost, often through ways we do not expect, in His time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mithredath, the Persian treasurer, counted out the sacred vessels into Sheshbazzar's hands. A pagan officer becomes a faithful steward, guarding what belonged to the God of Israel. The kingdom of heaven often relies on unlikely custodians doing honest work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty platters of gold, a thousand of silver, twenty-nine knives, thirty bowls, four hundred ten silver bowls—the exact count recorded. Every piece mattered, every vessel precious. What God cherishes, He accounts for. Nothing is too small to be remembered or restored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five thousand four hundred vessels brought from captivity to home. Readers today hear an echo in restoration—how the Lord gathers back what was scattered, returns the faithful to their deepest purpose, and lets us carry home what was lost. His restoration is thorough and personal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
